name: SourceControl - Git Reimplemented in Go
tagline: Production-grade Git implementation from scratch in pure Go 🔧
description: Fully-functional version control system reimplementing Git's core internals in Go without wrapping git commands. Implements content-addressable object storage, Merkle tree structures, binary index format, and complete CLI with 16,354 lines of tests achieving 121% test-to-code ratio for production reliability.

keyFeatures.title: Content-Addressable Object Store with SHA-1
keyFeatures.description: Custom implementation of Git's sharded directory structure (.source/objects/ab/cdef...) with type-safe wrappers for ObjectHash, CompressedData, and SerializedObject. Implements DEFLATE compression, lazy hash computation with caching, and atomic write operations using write-rename pattern to prevent corruption during crashes.

keyFeatures.title: Concurrent Tree Building with Adaptive Parallelism
keyFeatures.description: Generic worker pool using Go 1.18+ generics with panic recovery, context cancellation, and smart concurrency threshold (≥3 subdirectories triggers parallel processing via errgroup, otherwise sequential to avoid goroutine overhead). Converts hierarchical file systems to Git's flat tree object model recursively.

keyFeatures.title: Binary Index Format with O(1) Lookups
keyFeatures.description: Implements Git's staging area binary format with dual data structure approach - maintains sorted slice for Git compatibility and concurrent hash map (entryMap) for constant-time file lookups during staging operations. Includes SHA-1 checksum validation and atomic serialization to disk.

keyFeatures.title: Type-Safe Path System and Config Hierarchy
keyFeatures.description: Strongly-typed path abstractions (AbsolutePath, RelativePath, RepositoryPath, SourcePath) prevent path mixing bugs. Thread-safe hierarchical config manager with RWMutex supporting 5-level precedence (CLI flags → repo → user → system → defaults) and concurrent config file loading via errgroup.
